reasonPack.formatSelection: 136+251-6 (inspected 720p H.264 video plus Opus audio; normalized to MP4/M4A)
reasonPack.publicationBoundary: Only derived transcript, source VTT, and this public receipt are published. Local video, audio, raw source metadata, and the private manifest are not published.

derivation.captionAcquisition: The built-in ReasonPack caption command did not retain a track and began local Whisper fallback. That run was stopped; a separate yt-dlp en-orig VTT fetch succeeded. The source VTT and transcript were inserted into the completed media pack, its manifest and sums were regenerated, and ReasonPack verify passed.
derivation.transcript.txt: Incremental lines in the ReasonPack VTT (cue lines with word-level timestamp tags), HTML entities decoded, grouped by 30-second cue start; no wording correction or speaker attribution.
derivation.verification: ReasonPack closed-manifest SHA-256 verification, followed by SHA-256 calculation of public files.

editorial.verdict: Take the core lesson seriously; watch selected passages, not necessarily the full 44:50 interview. Start with a reversible, checkable task. Seek a separate deployment and security playbook before broader access.
editorial.thesis: Good agent work depends on closing the loop from intent to inspectable behavior, not merely giving longer instructions.

recommendedSegments.why: First-person failure story about spec-driven work in a video editor.
First-person account of improving the agent environment with app interaction and screenshots.
Start small, observe the agent, expand trust with evidence, and prefer checkable tasks.

claimMap.finding: Pocock says agents need explicit priorities and a well-maintained codebase.
claimMap.limit: No comparative study in the interview.

claimMap.finding: He says he uses agent teaching as an introduction before reading primary material.
claimMap.limit: The practice is described, not independently audited.

claimMap.finding: He reports his video-editor code and agent results worsened while centering a large spec.
claimMap.limit: One project, no shared logs or controlled comparison.

claimMap.finding: He reports better results after agents could run and inspect his application.
claimMap.limit: No before/after quality metric or artifacts in the interview.

claimMap.finding: He describes multiple agents and hundreds of commits per day.
claimMap.limit: Commit count is not a quality or value measure; not independently checked here.

claimMap.finding: He recommends supervised, small tasks before widening agent scope.
claimMap.limit: Permission, approval, and rollback controls are GhostMesh recommendations.

claimMap.finding: He suggests a client-specific prototype and acknowledges limited experience competing without a large audience.
claimMap.limit: Not a validated sales strategy; an aside about billing should not be treated as guidance.
